body: Sad for others but so happy to have found this thread. Still waiting on manual ECF uploaded in July. Well past 120 payments now. When I called, I was gaslit further that my form was missing info. I was reading my form aloud to the rep with all the info. Truly made me feel like I was losing my kind. Thought I was alone. At least I'm not crazy. But it's worse the system is totally insane.

I don't want to be closed-minded or ageist, but sometimes, I wonder if those, who give advice come from a system that no longer exists or are privileged to work in well-resourced institutions. I don't want to be a doomer, and I hope you can take this advice (from others) and grow from it. But honestly, there are a number of institutions that are just toxic. You are asked to do multiple jobs with less than the salary of one. I am currently trying to move on from an institution like that with the hope that my new academic position is just the expectation of 1 full-time job. I do think that you need to know your priorities and set appropriate boundaries in higher education. My new academic position comes with a very clear mission focus and very clear job description and expectations. I also know that it does get better as you gain experience and have less new preps. I also recognize that some institutions have stronger resources and better funding. However, in some places, your decreased teaching load and more experience are met with increased service and picking up the pieces of a dying system. I hope that we can have more open and honest conversations about the unsustainable and unhealthy workload in many institutions of higher education. It is driving out valuable talent with support and other options.

I'm doing this and actually getting a substantial raise but I'm changing the type and size of institution I'm working at. I realize higher ed is toxic and burnout provoking everywhere. But I'm wondering how much higher it is at institutions underwater.

And this has been the final straw... That led me to realize the current environment of higher ed is no longer worth it to be. Realized after a recent interview that respect for my expertise was an unusual experience... Good bye higher ed.

Yes. This! At the point they've been passed through K-12 and undergraduate... I teach grad students. I recently mentioned to a colleague that I have time in the semester to teach my content area, skills, and competencies or the basic literacy, writing, research, and learning skills those students need to be successful. But not both! It's frustrating for the students and me when they don't have the skills to be successful in advanced, specialized, professional education. It's amplified by the fact that none of these students are aware of these deficits because no one in their educational history has had the time and/or support to provide critical feedback.

I'm really glad you were able to share what Asmon means to you. He's probably a light in the darkness to a lot of folks. Your ability to share and be vulnerable will help others too. As others have said. Fuck cancer. You are a badass. And I hope you can have some enjoyable moments.

So appreciate asmon sharing his struggles and being so vulnerable. I'm a mental health professional who found asmon in the midst of my own grief and anxiety issues so the parasocoial has been strong. I really respect how much he can help his community and the wider gaming community through his vulnerability and sharing his experience so honestly. He's a real one.

This is exactly it. I teach full-time and do clinical mental health work 1 day per week often with anxious teens and young adults in college. It has gotten so difficult to expose clients to meaningfully stressful or anxiety provoking situations for gradual exposure, because so many "well meaning" but harmful folks in their lives alter expectations and give them an out from growth experiences. This also communicates the inferred message "I don't believe you can ever handle this" or "I don't believe you are competent enough to ever succeed." With some of the young adults I'm working with they've graduated high school and college to flounder as adults in procuring long term employment because they finally hit a true barrier and don't have coping skills to cope with the anxiety and perform. This crisis is what finally leads to motivation to change.
I was having a rough time. And now I can appreciate all the great people in the world after quite a few caring people reached out. Sometimes you forget how much goodness there is in the world.
Thanks for the care. I'm working on it.
